method: several rounds as arm x year interactions
layout: arm x round interactions down the rows (CSH*2014, CSH*2015, TUP*2014, TUP*2015), outcomes across columns
placebo row that looks like an effect (CSH*2014)
year-effect rows with stars that look like effects (2014, 2015)
tags.picture_matters: The text layer shifts the Savings column down one row (0.45, the control mean, lands on the CSH*2014 line, 0.03 on TUP*2014, 0.22 on TUP*2015, 0.43 on 2014), misplaces values in LandCult, drops every star, and turns the subscripted labels beta_2014^TUP - beta^CSH into '2T0U14P - CSH'. Row-to-value pairing must come from the picture.

context_needed: South Sudan (Yei County), BRAC Targeting the Ultra-Poor pilot; Chowdhury, Collins, Ligon and Munshi (2016). Women from a 2013 census were randomised into TUP (productive asset transfer of about $240, training, food transfers), UCT (cash of the same total value, $350-$410) and control (PDF p. 4). Baseline 2013; midline June 2014; endline mid-2015. Specification (PDF p. 5): outcome on year effects, arm x year interactions and the 2013 value of the outcome. Because conflict delayed the cash, it was paid only after the June 2014 survey, so TUP*2014 is the effect 3-6 months after the asset transfers, TUP*2015 the effect at 15-18 months, CSH*2015 the effect about 12 months after the cash, and CSH*2014 is a placebo (a second baseline for the cash group). Outcomes are shares of households with a positive value (header '% > 0').

not_stored.reason: pre-programme gap: the cash had not yet been paid at the 2014 survey, and the authors call this interaction a placebo (PDF p. 5)
year effects (round intercepts), not programme effects, despite their stars
coefficients on the baseline value of the outcome and on the missing-baseline dummy: covariates

rule: When arms and rounds run down the rows as arm x year interactions, each interaction is one stored effect with the arm in arm and the round in time_point. Not every interaction is an effect: an arm whose transfers came after a round gives a placebo for that round, and the bare year rows are intercepts. Their stars do not make them effects. A row that contrasts two programme arms (for example T3 minus T2) is stored with effect_type 'difference between arms', naming both arms in arm.

resolved_questions.question: The beta^TUP - beta^CSH rows are differences between the asset-transfer arm and the cash arm, printed without an SE; the CSH term is presumably the 2015 cash effect (the text tests beta_TUP,t - beta_Cash,2015), but the table label does not say so. Same question as for other arm-difference rows: store (with what effect_type), or leave out?
resolved_questions.resolution: Decided by Lucas, 22 Nov 2026: store the beta_TUP - beta_CSH rows, labelled 'difference between arms'.
